alignment.note: Greek combines a finite verb of motion (ἦλθεν) with a present participle (κηρύσσων), 'he went preaching'. The Vulgate renders a periphrastic imperfect erat prædicans ('he was preaching'), dropping the verb of motion, and the Peshitta uses the periphrastic ܘܡܟܪܙ ܗܘܐ (participle + auxiliary 'was') likewise lacking the motion verb; both versions thus flatten the Greek 'came/went + preaching' into a single durative 'was preaching'.

Greek εἰς ('into') with the synagogues is matched by Vulgate in synagogis (locative ablative, 'in'); the Peshitta expresses the locative by the prefixed preposition ܒ on ܒܟܠܗܝܢ, so no separate token corresponds, while the directional force of εἰς is softened to a static locative in both versions.
Pronominal 'their' is suffixed on the Syriac noun ܟܢܘܫܬܗܘܢ rather than standing as a separate token.

The second εἰς ('into all Galilee') is rendered by Vulgate et in, with the Latin adding the connective et absent in Greek at this point; the Peshitta again encodes the preposition as the prefix ܒ on ܒܟܠܗ, leaving no discrete particle to align.
τὰ δαιμόνια / ܫܐܕܐ / dæmonia; the Greek article has no counterpart in the anarthrous Syriac and Latin forms but the reference is identical.
ἐκβάλλων / ܘܡܦܩ ('and casting out') / ejiciens; the Greek closing pilcrow ¶ marks a paragraph break with no versional equivalent.
